# Independent review: KPS coefficient interface and Bernstein control

Date: 2026-09-17.
Reviewer: /root/pairzero_geometry_review.
Verdict: ACCEPT_LIMITED_KPS_INTERFACE_AND_BF_CONTROL.
Disposition: no correction required for the bounded claims K1--K4.
Scope: isolated PAPER mathematics; no source-sign or RH conclusion.

## 1. Exact bytes and sources

The complete final candidate was reread after its editorial section-2
revision:
`KPS_MOMENT_INTERFACE.md`, 10782 bytes, 231 LF,
SHA256 `5ece10af57e06d233cb501ae2ea6aff4ba4dacf4409ea0a76b1a75a49b1b4231`.
The earlier assigned hash `390c50ea23310f697ace7ac9c2f625b092cfadec8d0909f61b7057496c5bbba6`
is superseded. The mathematical K1--K4 claims are unchanged.

pp416--417 for the proof interface; p419 for reference [25]; and p382

## 2. K1: normalization, coefficients and the actual theorem domain

PASS; final candidate lines 10--79.

The substitution t=exp(2x) gives

    int_R Phi(x)exp(izx)dx
      =(1/2) M_r(5/4+iz/2)=xi(1/2+iz).

At z=0 this proves Z=xi(1/2)>0 from the positive source integral. The
normalization q=Phi/Z therefore gives F(0)=1, precisely the constant
coefficient of the KPS series. Its positive Fourier sign is consistent
with the displayed xi argument; evenness also identifies the opposite
sign. This L1 normalization does not alter the separately fixed L2
normalization used in the original V.

Full-source tails dominate exp(R|x|) for every finite R. Thus termwise
expansion and differentiation are locally uniformly justified, and
F(z)=sum (-1)^n mu_(2n)z^(2n)/(2n)! is entire. Every even moment is
strictly positive because q is a positive nondegenerate density.
Comparing adjacent coefficients in the normalized KPS product gives
exactly

    Psi(n)=(2n)(2n-1)mu_(2n-2)/mu_(2n),
    phi(n)=Psi(n)/n=2(2n-1)mu_(2n-2)/mu_(2n).

Conversely, the product of these fixed ratios telescopes to 1/a_n,
with a_0=1, so the resulting series agrees with F everywhere. This
converse is a statement about specified integer values, not a claim
that an admissible interpolation exists.

The journal's Theorem 4.4 explicitly states that phi in B_P1 implies
Psi(u)=u phi(u) belongs to N_D and J_Psi belongs to D_L intersect D_P.
The definition includes Bernstein--Pick structure and the displayed
1-separation conditions. Thus there is no missing additional N_D premise
in the proposed sufficient implication. Ordinary Bernstein membership
would not satisfy that theorem. Theorem 4.1 has the distinct N_D premise
and a weaker van Dantzig conclusion. The paper expressly leaves the xi
interpolation question unresolved on p397. The detailed auxiliary input
[25] is listed as a 2022 working paper; the candidate correctly treats
Theorem 4.4 as a published external theorem, not a proof reproduced here.

The author-derived coefficients avoid reliance on the paper's equations
(4.15)--(4.18) or a potentially different centered-xi normalization.
If the required B_P1 interpolant were independently constructed, its
real-zero conclusion for F would put every xi zero on Re(s)=1/2. This
is a correct conditional implication. Neither existence nor necessity
of this sufficient subclass for RH is asserted.

## 3. K2: strict growth, paid endpoints and covariance differentiation

PASS; final candidate lines 83--127.

The pinned Csordas--Varga statement, after its exact scaling, is strict
concavity of ell(s)=log Phi(sqrt(s)) on (0,infinity). For a differentiable
strictly concave function, the derivative is strictly decreasing: equality
at two distinct points, together with monotonicity, would force an affine
segment and contradict strict concavity. Thus h=-ell' is strictly increasing.
This argument does not infer ell''<0 at every point.

Evenness and smoothness give Phi'(x)=O(x) near zero, so
rho'(s)=Phi'(sqrt(s))/(2sqrt(s)) stays bounded there, while rho(0)>0.
At infinity, rho and rho' inherit decay faster than any power from the
full source bounds. Consequently M(p) is finite for p>0 and all the
weighted logarithmic integrals used below converge locally uniformly
for u>1/2. The substitution s=x^2 also verifies
mu_(2n)=M(n+1/2)/Z and Z=M(1/2), with no extra factor of two.

For p=u-1/2>0, both limits of s^p rho(s) are zero. Integration by parts
therefore proves pM(p)=-int s^p rho'(s)ds, without a missing endpoint.
Dividing by M(p+1) gives the stated expectation under the probability
density s^p rho(s)/M(p+1). In particular, b(u)>0 directly from the positive
moment ratio, without needing a separate pointwise positivity assertion
about h.

For differentiation, h rho=-rho'. Thus integrability of h and h log(s)
under the tilted law follows from the bounds on rho'; the denominator
and its logarithmic derivative are controlled by rho. Differentiating
numerator and denominator gives exactly b'(u)=4 Cov(h(S),log S).
All absolute first products needed for the two-independent-copy identity
are finite. Since h and log are strictly increasing and the law has a
positive density, the product of their two differences is positive
whenever S differs from S', an event of probability one. The covariance
is strictly positive.

Hence 0<b_1<b_2<... . Cross multiplication of adjacent ratios yields
exactly (9), with factor (2n-1)/(2n+1). This is genuine actual-source
information. It pays monotonicity only: it proves neither further
Bernstein derivative signs nor Pick analyticity nor pole/zero separation.
No Levy representation follows merely from writing b as an expectation.

## 4. K3: the explicit Bernstein control and its two exact obstructions

PASS; final candidate lines 131--180.

Gaussian integration gives Z0=sqrt(pi)(1-a), a=2^(-5/2), and

    mu^0_(2n)=(2n)!/(4^n n!) * (1-a2^(-n))/(1-a).

Substitution into the coefficient ratios cancels the factorials to give
exactly b^0_n=4(1-a2^(1-n))/(1-a2^(-n)). Geometric expansion of phi0 gives

    phi0(u)=4-4 sum_(k>=1) a^k exp(-k log(2)u).

Subtracting its value at zero yields precisely the finite positive
atomic Levy measure in (11). Its positive constant term and finite
positive jump masses establish the full Bernstein property, with all
derivative signs; the sums may be differentiated to every order on
u>=0 because sum a^k k^j converges for each j.

The denominator vanishes exactly at the listed lattice of points
u=-5/2+2pi i j/log(2); changing the sign of j lists the same set. Each
zero is simple and the unfactored numerator 1-2a2^(-u) equals -1 there.
The poles in the upper half-plane are consequently nonremovable. A
Pick extension compatible with the Bernstein function near the positive
axis would agree on an open intersection and, by analytic continuation
on the connected upper half-plane minus these isolated poles, would
have to reproduce them. This contradicts holomorphy of a Pick function.
Thus the non-Pick conclusion does not rely on a numerical failure test.

The exact Fourier transform F0 also agrees with the pinned dual filter.
Factoring its numerator gives the zero equation
z^2=-8log(a)-16pi i j. Every j!=0 gives nonreal zeros. It therefore
refutes replacing the B_P1 hypothesis by ordinary Bernstein interpolation
even on this positive, even, strictly squared-coordinate-log-concave
source class. It is not the theta source and does not share all its
source hypotheses.

Differentiating Psi0=u phi0 twice gives exactly the displayed Psi0'' series. If u>2/log(2), each
summand is strictly negative because k log(2)>=log(2). Therefore Psi0
is not convex. Formula (4.1) in the journal gives nonnegative second
derivative for every spectrally negative Levy exponent, so Psi0 cannot
belong to N, hence cannot belong to N_D. The weaker Theorem 4.1 cannot
be applied to this control under a hidden domain assumption either.
The previously accepted negative full-V row concerns this control only.

## 5. K4: uniqueness from a finite Hausdorff moment measure

PASS; final candidate lines 184--201.

For a Bernstein function with usual Levy measure nu,
int min(1,r)nu(dr)<infinity. Therefore
int exp(-r)(1-exp(-r))nu(dr)<infinity: near zero the weight is O(r),
and on the tail it is bounded while nu has finite tail mass.
The pushforward sigma under t=exp(-r), plus the drift mass B at t=1,
is consequently a finite positive measure on [0,1].

For every n>=1 its (n-1)-st moment is exactly
phi(n+1)-phi(n). The n=1 increment includes the zeroth moment, so all
Hausdorff moments, including total mass, are known. Equality of integer
values gives equality of these moment measures by polynomial density
in C([0,1]). There is no missing moment of order zero.

The pushed jump measure has no atom at 1 since r>0, and no atom at 0
since no finite r maps there. Its mass at 1 therefore identifies B.
On (0,1), division by the strictly positive weight t(1-t) recovers the
pushforward of nu, even if that unweighted measure is infinite near an
endpoint. Inverting the bijection r -> exp(-r) recovers nu itself.
Finally phi(1) fixes the killing/constant term A; its defining integral
is finite by the Levy condition.

This proves uniqueness among Bernstein interpolants of all positive
integer values. Applied to (10), the existing phi0 is the unique such
interpolant, and its non-Pick property rules out another Bernstein--Pick
interpolant with the same data. It does not establish existence for the
actual theta sequence, nor uniqueness among arbitrary analytic functions.

## Final disposition

ACCEPT_LIMITED_KPS_INTERFACE_AND_BF_CONTROL, bound to final candidate
SHA256 `5ece10af57e06d233cb501ae2ea6aff4ba4dacf4409ea0a76b1a75a49b1b4231`.
No correction is required. The editorial revision preserves the theorem's
real domain and the explicit interpolation gap.

K1 is a closed conditional coefficient interface. K2 supplies a strict
first inequality from a proved actual-source property. K3--K4 rigorously
exclude a weaker Bernstein-only substitute and a change of Bernstein
interpolant for the given control. The finite diagnostic plays no role
in any of these conclusions. Actual B_P1 membership, full V positivity
and RH are unproved; no new Pro proof request or canonical admission is
justified by this review.

# Parent analytic check: KPS interface

Candidate SHA256 5ece10af57e06d233cb501ae2ea6aff4ba4dacf4409ea0a76b1a75a49b1b4231.
This check is independent algebra and analytic domain checking. It is not a
finite diagnostic used as a universal proof.

1. Normalization: with t=exp(2x), Phi(x)dx is exactly
(1/2)t^(1/4)r(t)dt. Including exp(izx) changes the Mellin argument to
5/4+iz/2, so M_r=2xi(2s-2) gives xi(1/2+iz). Thus Z=xi(1/2) and no
factor 2 or pi is missing. The unmodified V retains its L2 normalization.
A positive L1 normalization is used only for the coefficient sequence.

2. Neighboring coefficients of F are mu_(2n)/(2n)!. Their ratio is
(2n)(2n-1)mu_(2n-2)/mu_(2n). Division by n gives exactly the asserted
b_n. Conversely product ratios telescope to a_n since a_0=1. The
KPS paper defines exactly this J_Psi series. Its Theorem 4.4 has the
additional global Bernstein-Pick and unit-separation hypotheses; its
Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.7 do not pay that hypothesis. No formula
in the Riemann interpolation subsection is used as an input identity.

3. The substitution s=x^2 in the even moment integral gives
mu_(2n)=M(n+1/2)/M(1/2), so b(u)=4p M(p)/M(p+1), p=u-1/2.
At zero, Phi(x)=Phi(0)+O(x^2) implies rho(s)=Phi(0)+O(s), with bounded
rho' locally. At infinity the differentiable full theta tail beats every
polynomial in s and every power of log s, including the derivative of
rho. Therefore s^p rho(s) vanishes at both ends for p>0 and IBP is exact.
The same bounds with |log s| factors permit differentiating on compact
subintervals u>1/2. In the covariance identity h*rho=-rho', so no hidden
integrability assumption on an unweighted growing h is required.
Strict concavity of differentiable ell makes h=-ell' strictly increasing:
equal derivative values at two points would force affinity on that
interval. Independent-copy symmetrization proves strictly positive
covariance with log s, since the density is everywhere positive.
Rearranging b_(n+1)>b_n gives the stated Turan coefficient (2n-1)/(2n+1).
This proves only monotonicity, not the higher derivative signs.

4. For the control, integral x^(2n)exp(-beta x^2)dx equals
Gamma(n+1/2)beta^(-n-1/2). Subtracting the beta=2 contribution with
factor 1/4 gives mu0=(2n)!/(4^n n!)*(1-a 2^(-n))/(1-a).
The normalized coefficient ratio is therefore 4(1-2a 2^(-n))/(1-a2^(-n)).
Expanding q/(1-q) with q=a2^(-u), |q|<1 for u>=0, yields the finite
positive Levy measure 4sum a^k delta_(k log2), and the nonnegative constant
4(1-2a)/(1-a). All differentiated series converge absolutely locally.
Poles satisfy exp(-u log2)=1/a, giving the vertical lattice (12), with
nonzero numerator. Such upper-half-plane poles preclude Pick continuation.
Twice differentiating u phi0 shows negative second derivative for
u>2/log2, proving failure of convexity needed for a spectrally negative
Levy exponent. This does not misuse KPS Theorem 4.1.

5. A BF increment at integer n is B plus the (n-1)-th moment of the
finite pushed-forward measure t(1-t)nu on (0,1). Including B at t=1
makes all increments one Hausdorff moment sequence, starting at order zero.
Moment uniqueness on [0,1] determines that measure, then B, then nu on
(0,1) by division by t(1-t), and the value at 1 determines A. There is no
missing atom at t=0, which would correspond to an infinite jump not in
the BF representation. Hence phi0 is the only BF interpolant of the
control data. Arbitrary holomorphic interpolants are not covered.

6. The KPS theorem is a named published input, with source text checked,
not a claim to have independently reconstructed all cited background.
Our q-specific missing Pick/interlacing assertions stay unproved. The
finite diagnostic has truncated modes/range and no certified error;
it is excluded from every proof. Source-sign progress, RH proof/refutation,
negative actual V witness, canonical admission, and counter reset are all false.
accepted: Exact normalized KPS coefficient interface for the original full theta Fourier transform
Strict monotonicity of required moment ratios for all positive integer orders from the pinned Csordas--Varga concavity
Gaussian-difference control admits a genuine Bernstein interpolation but has non-Pick poles and nonreal Fourier zeros
Uniqueness of Bernstein interpolation on all positive integers excludes a different Pick repair for that control

scope_limits: Source PF plus reciprocity has not supplied the missing complex condition
No change in full V sign frontier
Finite diagnostic excluded from proof and not certified
No new Proshka proof request justified
